risks.note: The MD&A states that all activities of the Company during the year related to this one business and that there are no separate reportable segments, so there is no second earnings stream to absorb a demand or pricing shock in media monitoring. Reported turnover fell to Rs. 232.27 Lakhs from Rs. 316.27 Lakhs in the previous year.
risks.risk: Single-activity concentration — the entire business is "Media Monitoring" related services

risks.note: The MD&A ratio commentary attributes the swing in Net Profit Ratio (from (114.66) to 20.51) and in Return on Capital Employed (from (26.35) to 78.61) 'mainly on account of write back of loan during the year ended 31st March, 2026', and states that Net Capital Turnover, Debt Equity and Return on Net Worth are 'not applicable on account of negative working capital and networth'. Operating performance therefore does not underpin the reported return.
risks.risk: Earnings quality — FY26 profit rests on a loan write-back, against negative net worth and negative working capital

risks.note: Management explicitly flags 'ensuring continued access to critical data sources' as a key risk and names 'potential restrictions on data access from digital platforms' as a threat. The product is built on content the Company does not own, so a platform-side restriction directly removes input supply.
risks.risk: Dependence on continued access to third-party data sources

risks.note: 'Protecting its digital infrastructure from cybersecurity threats' is listed among key risks and 'increasing cybersecurity risks' among threats; for a wholly digital monitoring and analytics operation, an infrastructure compromise interrupts service delivery and client data.

Management flags 'maintaining competitiveness in a rapidly evolving market' and 'adapting to technological changes', with competition and rapid technological advancement named as threats that 'could impact its market position, operational efficiency, compliance costs, and overall profitability'. The Company is simultaneously attempting a transition to an AI-powered platform, so the pace of adoption is a live execution risk.
risks.risk: Technology change and competitive intensity in an AI-led market

risks.note: The FY26 Form MR-3 report qualifies compliance with a list of observations: the Nomination and Remuneration Committee is not constituted as required under Section 178 (it includes an executive director); 100% of promoter and promoter-group shareholding is not dematerialised (LODR clause 31(2)); the names of all independent directors do not appear in the IICA independent-director data bank (Section 150); the Company's website is not updated as required under Regulation 46; newspaper advertisements of results for three quarters lacked the QR code and webpage details required by Regulation 47(1); the outcome of the 28 May 2025 board meeting was not uploaded to the stock exchange; and annual listing fees were not paid within the prescribed 30 days for FY 2025-26.
risks.risk: Statutory compliance and governance lapses flagged by the Secretarial Auditor

risks.note: The Secretarial Auditor reports outstanding unsecured loans from an erstwhile director and a member, including amounts received after cessation of directorship and loans accepted under the Companies Act, 1956, concluding that 'the Company has not fully complied with the provisions of Sections 73 and 74 of the Companies Act, 2013 in respect of acceptance and repayment of deposits/amounts deemed to be deposits'. It also records that the Statutory Auditors reported qualifications/observations in the FY26 audit report. Separately, the AGM notice discloses that the statutory auditors, M/s N. A Shah & Associates, resigned on 14 May 2026, creating a casual vacancy filled by M/s S.K. Patodia & Associates LLP.
risks.risk: Deemed-deposit non-compliance and qualified statutory audit

risks.note: The AGM notice seeks a special resolution for remuneration totalling up to Rs. 2,00,00,000 to the Managing Director and Executive Director for three financial years effective 22 April 2026, expressly payable 'in excess of the minimum limits and conditions mentioned in Schedule V' in case of inadequacy of profits; the explanatory statement sets minimum remuneration of Rs. 45,00,000 for the Managing Director and Rs. 37,00,000 for the Executive Director. This is a fixed, board-approved cash cost set against a company reporting turnover of Rs. 232.27 Lakhs and negative net worth.
risks.risk: Managerial remuneration payable in excess of statutory limits despite inadequate profits
